title: Built and killed a lot of strategies using claude. These are the 2 I'm actually running on MNQ right now
author: LessAdeptness5935
selftext:
Been building and throwing away strategies on MNQ for a while. Most die in testing. I tried retest entries, divergence entries, basic buy and sell one contract hold, New york ORB, and some others, I have all pine scripts saved. Ive taken about 2 automated payouts. one for 500 and one for 1000. Fully automated fully passed the account and taken payout(2-3 weeks). But then also blew my accounts right after. These two survived and are the only ones I have wired up live right now, so here's the whole thing including the numbers I don't love. Im trying to have a running strategy that can hold multiple funded accounts without risking blowing them. 

**The pipeline**

TradingView (Pine v5) -> alert with {{strategy.order.alert_message}} -> TradersPost webhook -> prop account. 

A third alert forks to a Google Apps Script -> Sheet -> my own journaling app so every fill is logged independent of the broker. This journaling file is more so a TradingHub idea I had also thought up. Having a dedicated area of space for prop firm trading, with a news calender, whatever the average trader would need to be omnipresent with the market as well as add any of their sites, not needing to scroll through many tabs. that was the idea. Still building upon this and would love some insight. 

---

**1. EMA Pullback Structure Strategy

MNQ 5m, long and short. Enters once at full size, exits in three sized legs: a quick TP, a runner, and a bigger target. Force-flat at 12:50 PT so nothing is held overnight.


2. Stik MR(Stochastic Mean Reversion)

MNQ daily, long only, mean reversion. Scales into as many as 4 units on successively deeper dips. Holds overnight and over weekends, which is exactly why it can never run on a funded prop account - Topstep force-flats at 3:10pm CT and an overnight position is an instant violation. It runs on a dead account as a signal target only. Would need a live account with 5-10K drawdown to safely run. This scales up though, compounding interest.

There is one issue I ran into. I could only run backtesting on tradingview 5min for 7 weeks back. So I built a backtesting engine with Claude, primarily for pine scripts. Has some issues here and there with running some concepts but its easily fixable.


Me and some friends also set up a little discord for a community dedicated for prop firm algo trading help. We also set up a discord News Bot that delivers real time important news dedicated for MNQ,MGC,ES and other futures indexes. 

This post is simply a reach out and share of my work so far. Would love to hear feedback and speak on this concept further! If you wanna interact with all the things in this post join this discord or just reply here.

https://discord.gg/qBgTQcxDu

comments.author: Interesting_Gold_792
comments.body:
The part that caught my attention isn’t really the EMA itself — it’s that you were able to get payouts and then blow the accounts afterward.

That makes me wonder whether the bigger problem is the risk layer rather than the entry logic.

Have you broken down the failures by things like:

\- regime / volatility at the time  
\- max adverse excursion before the loss  
\- consecutive-loss clusters  
\- position size relative to remaining drawdown  
\- whether the strategy behaved differently after a payout or during volatile opens

If the same setup can make it through a payout but later violate the account, I’d be really interested in whether a separate portfolio-level risk governor could preserve the edge without changing the signal itself.

Also, logging fills independently from the broker is a good idea. I’d keep rejected/blocked trades in that journal too — those can become really useful counterfactual data later.

replies.author: LessAdeptness5935
replies.body:
My experience with the payouts and the profitability is having as least amount of rules when it comes to risk. With the Stochastic mean reversion strategy(my favorite one), it holds throughout all adverse excursions adding cons until we see a positive move in our direction, which then we will dump all cons. The first payout I took was with a one contract hold all day, and the next one was from this EMA pullback structure. I would love to talk to you about this more and share my strategies. Send me a dm on discord im St1kk1d. I could see a daily stop loss and take profit working but i have yet to figure it out. Position size relative to remaining drawdown is an amazing idea as well as regime/volatility at the time. If I can recognize different volatilities, assign heavier or lighter contracts. that could be optimal.   
The logging journal works with google sheets, using Apps Scripts and then my tradinghub reads that and logs all the Daily trades.

replies.author: Interesting_Gold_792
replies.body:
That actually explains a lot.

The stochastic mean-reversion strategy is the one I’d be most interested in stress-testing, because adding contracts through adverse excursion can work extremely well until you hit the regime where mean reversion simply doesn’t arrive fast enough.

I don’t think I’d necessarily change the signal logic first. I’d probably put an independent risk governor around it.

Something like:

remaining account drawdown + current MAE + realized volatility + total accumulated size

\-> determines whether another scale-in is allowed and how large it can be.

That way the strategy can still express the mean-reversion idea, but it can’t keep increasing exposure indefinitely while the original thesis is going against it.

Have you tested the scale-ins during your worst trending/high-volatility periods specifically?

I’d also be curious whether the accounts that blew had one large adverse sequence or multiple smaller loss clusters. That distinction could tell you whether a daily stop is enough or whether the position-level scaling itself needs a cap.

And yeah, I’d be happy to keep comparing notes here. I’m working on a system too, so this kind of risk-layer discussion is exactly what interests me.
